meta.description: Kickoff 59, the check at the peak phase on a second calibration day on ibm_kingston, in two jobs, as Kickoff 57's. T_M.definition: from the end of M's first H (its first sx) to the start of its last H (its last sx), in the wait test without refocusing (W-no) as scheduled by manacitra.wait.scheduled on the live target

fixed_before_the_data.rule: the revised rule at the peak phase: a cell is one chain at its phi*, informative if its loss_R1 interval lies entirely above informative_floor; DISAGREE if any informative cell's d1 interval lies entirely outside [-margin, +margin]; AGREE if every informative cell's lies entirely inside; NOT SETTLED otherwise; with no informative cell, the verdict carries ", uninformative". d1(phi*) = F_no(phi*) - F_ref (1 - loss_R1(phi*)), loss = M's P(1) minus its P(1) in Z, F against the wait test's phi = 0 parity ideal. phi* = 180 - theta_R1, wrapped to [0, 360) and rounded to the nearest whole degree, from job 1's fit (OLS of M's P(1) over the six phases, theta_R1 = atan2(s, -b)), recorded before job 2 was built
fixed_before_the_data.bootstraps: the verdict's: Kickoff 53's analysis (analyse_53.py, byte-identical) on the phi* circuits, W-ref and Z only, the phi* circuits labelled phase 0 for the call, seed bootstrap, n_boot draws, chain by chain in the drawn order: F for W-no(phi*) and W-ref (the copies with replacement, each redrawn from a multinomial), then P(1) for Z, R0(phi*), R1(phi*) (the copies with replacement, each redrawn binomially). Beside the verdict, analyse_57.py's joint generator with the same seed: it first repeats the verdict's draws, which must equal them exactly, then continues: per M, W-no(+90), R0(+90), R1(+90); then job 1's R1 at the six phases per M (the copies with replacement, each redrawn binomially), refitting on every resample

design.peak_procedure: Kickoff 57's analyse_57.peaks, unchanged: OLS of M's P(1) over the six phases (analyse_52.fit, theta_R); theta_R1 = atan2(s, -b); phi* = 180 - theta_R1 wrapped to [0, 360), rounded to the nearest whole degree (halves up); from the point estimate

draw_on_snapshot.procedure: k59-rule.md: candidates on the live target's CZ edges (either direction), L1 != L3; exclusions (a qubit of Kickoffs 55 to 58; operational; readout error above 3%; CZ error above 1%, the larger of the edge's listed directions; a missing value excludes); sort by (M, L1, L3); numpy.random.default_rng(5959).shuffle; take in order, skipping any chain that shares a qubit with one taken, until four

chain_draw.procedure: k59-rule.md: candidates on the live target's CZ edges (either direction), L1 != L3; exclusions (a qubit of Kickoffs 55 to 58; operational; readout error above 3%; CZ error above 1%, the larger of the edge's listed directions; a missing value excludes); sort by (M, L1, L3); numpy.random.default_rng(5959).shuffle; take in order, skipping any chain that shares a qubit with one taken, until four

peaks.rule: k59-rule.md: per chain, M's P(1) with the copies pooled; OLS fit c + b cos(phi) + s sin(phi) over the six phases; theta_R1 = atan2(s, -b); phi* = 180 - theta_R1, wrapped to [0, 360), rounded to the nearest whole degree; from the point estimate only
peaks.what: the peak phases, computed from job 1's counts by the rule's procedure and recorded at computed_utc, before job 2 was built (the job 2 records name this file by its SHA-256)

"""Kickoff 59 analysis, fixed before the data (sections 3 and 4 of the kickoff; k59-rule.md).

Kickoff 57's analysis, unchanged: analyse_57.py (a byte-identical copy) with its two seeds set to 59 as k59-rule.md fixes
them (analyse_57.SEED, the joint generator for the list beside the verdict, and analyse_53.SEED, the verdict's
bootstrap inside analyse_53.analyse). Everything else is analyse_57's:
- the peak phase from job 1 (analyse_57.peaks: OLS of M's P(1) over the six phases, theta_R1 = atan2(s, -b),
  phi* = 180 - theta_R1 wrapped to [0, 360) and rounded to the nearest whole degree, from the point estimate);
- the verdict on the four phi* cells by analyse_53.analyse (unchanged), seed 59, 10,000 draws, the copies drawn with
  replacement and each drawn copy's shots redrawn, phi* held fixed;
- beside it, from one generator (seed 59) that first repeats analyse_53's verdict draws and must equal them exactly:
  the check at +90 on the same chains, the original rule at phi* and at +90, job 1's fits with intervals, the drift.

Added here, beside the verdict (k59-rule.md, item 1): each waiting qubit's zero-wait baseline P(1) (Z), with its
interval from the verdict's bootstrap, and whether it exceeds 0.1. The verdict key analyse_57 names H57 is reported as
H59.

H59: DISAGREE if any informative cell's d1 interval lies entirely outside [-0.15, +0.15]; AGREE if every informative
cell's lies entirely inside; NOT SETTLED otherwise; ", uninformative" if no cell is informative.

Usage: python analyse_59.py                 (Kickoff 59's files)
       python analyse_59.py --synthetic     (analyse_57's synthetic tests, at seed 59)"""
from __future__ import annotations

A57.SEED = 59           # the joint generator beside the verdict (k59-rule.md)
A57.A53.SEED = 59       # the verdict's bootstrap (k59-rule.md)
Z_NOTE = 0.1


def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def analyse(labels1, counts1, labels2, counts2, order, phistar):
    r = A57.analyse(labels1, counts1, labels2, counts2, order, phistar)
    r["H59"] = r.pop("H57")
    r["zero_wait_baseline"] = {M: {"P1_Z": v["P1_Z"], "P1_Z_ci90": v["P1_Z_ci90"], "above_0.1": v["P1_Z"] > Z_NOTE} for M, v in r["chains"].items()}
    r["zero_wait_baseline_any_above_0.1"] = [M for M, v in r["zero_wait_baseline"].items() if v["above_0.1"]]
    return r
